title: Cache-stability is the real lever for memory/RAG token cost (v4 hypothesis)
summary: Extends orchestrator-token-cost-benchmark. Memory/RAG vendor "90% token savings" claims are true only vs. a strawman (full raw-history replay); vs. window+summary they collapse to ~30-50%, and can go NEGATIVE vs. a prompt-cached long context. Mechanism: prompt caching is prefix-based — any per-turn change invalidates everything downstream. Standard RAG re-queries/re-ranks each turn, so injected content changes → breaks the cache. Append-only memory (grow at the tail, never reorder/delete mid-session) keeps the prefix warm and only pays full price on the appended delta. CONSTRAINT specific to our harness: benchmark agents run via headless `claude -p`, so the Claude Code harness sets cache_control, NOT the orchestrator. The orchestrator's only lever is the STABILITY of content it injects through MCP tool results (get_learnings/search_knowledge/get_dependency_summaries): stable/append-only returns keep the agent's conversation prefix cacheable; re-ranked `search` returns vary the tool-result text each turn and break downstream cache. v4/v5 experiment: append-only stable context (lean) vs re-ranked replace context (search), measured on cache_read ratio + output-weighted NET cost at parity solve rate. Win only expected where memory is ACCUMULATIVE (notes/decisions) — not per-turn fresh query-specific retrieval, which caching beats anyway.
